LESSON: PLANTS • LEAVES • FLOWER • STEM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Neighbourhood
Topic 4.3: Plants • Leaves • Flower • Stem
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plants • Leaves • Flower • Stem, part of Our Neighbourhood in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have plants?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plants • Leaves • Flower • Stem together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner develops concepts of parts of a plant when exploring and manipulating parts of a plant.

Values:
Responsibility: learner enhances accountability and care for plants within the immediate environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental education: learner enhances environmental awareness when taking a nature walk round the school garden.

Link to other learning area:

Concepts of plants such as parts of plants (leaf) relates to concepts of leaf printing in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Realia-plants found within the environment, Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures and picture cut outs about plants

within the immediate environment, theme-based multi-purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices, songs and poems

about plants within the immediate environment, universal cuffs with padded pencils, crayons with grips, slant boards, foot- boards for learners using lower extremities, book holders and page turners, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table

tops are at a suitable height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/ crutches, head/ mouth pointers, splints for hands/ hand

stabilizers, adapted tools such as light hammers and saws with padded handles,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe

by writing/ mounting name cards

on parts of a plant.

parts of a plant.

seated/ positioned on devices

with worktops at a suitable

height and guided in purposive

different parts of a plant.

• Learners are guided in purposive

different parts of a plant from

74

• In purposive groups or pairs,

learners are guided to recite/

mime poems about parts of a

plant. Learners with speech

difficulties could alternatively

point the words of the poem in a

theme-based multi-purpose

communication board/ chart as

peers recite along.

• Learners are preferentially

seated/ positioned on devices

with worktops at a suitable

height and guided in purposive

groups or pairs to picture read on

parts of a plant from charts. The

pictures should be placed

mounted on cardboards or the

textbook be fastened to book

holders for ease of manipulation

using page turners. For learners

with difficulties in vision, the

pictures should be enlarged, with

brighter colour contrast and

placed on a slant board with an

inclination that is preferable by

the learner.

75

• In purposive groups, learners are

guided to take a nature walk or

move round the school garden

using appropriate mobility

devices with physical support to

identify work done by people.

Learners should be guided off

rugged/ slippery terrains and off

places with cold, fumes, heights

and dust to prevent triggering

conditions such as allergic

reaction and epileptic seizures

among learners who may have

the conditions.

• In purposive groups, learners

are guided to discuss/ share ideas

about the uses of plants (food,

beautify and shad
e) orally/ by

writing/ mounting relevant name

cards or by total communication.

• Learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided to

colour drawn pictures of parts of

a plant/ mount already prepared

picture cut-outs using any

functional part of the body or

76

appropriate Assistive technology

for manipulation, adapted

colouring tools with physical

support. Learners could use slant

boards, book holders and pencil

grips to perform the task.

Learners with tremors could

require splinting of the most

affected limb or use of hand

stabilizers. In severe cases,

learners with manipulation

difficulties could describe orally

the materials, choice of colour

and procedure for colouring as a

physical assistant does the actual

drawing under their instruction.

• Learners are guided individually

or in purposive pairs to mount

flowers on charts that are placed

on a flat surface which is at an

appropriate height. Learners

with manipulation difficulties

could mount using any

functional part of the body with

physical support.

• Learners are guided in purposive

77

pairs to display mounted pictures

of parts of a plant on the wall.

Learners with short stature could

be supported to use a class dais

to display the chart. Learners

with severe manipulation

difficulties could show peers

where and how to mount the

charts.

• Learners are strategically

positioned or preferentially

seated on positioning/ seating

devices whose worktops/ table

tops are at a suitable height and

guided to sort and group flowers

Assistive technology for

• Learners are guided in purposive

respectively using any functional

• Learners are appropriately

positioned and guided to sing/

on parts of plant or point the

peers sing along.

• In purposive groups or pairs,

seated on positioning/ seating

devices whose worktops/ table

guided to manipulate adapted

digital device by the use of any

functional part of the body or

appropriate Assistive technology

to watch and listen to video clips

on parts of plant.

• Learners are guided in pairs or

groups to water plants found in

the immediate environment

using appropriate Assistive

79

technology for movement and

manipulation for learners with

mobility and manipulation

difficulties, respectively.

Learners with brittle bone

disease should be guided to lift

light watering cans or maybe use

small cups to water plants so as

to prevent fractures. Learners

with epilepsy and those with

allergic reactions such as asthma

should be safeguarded from cold

or fumes as they perform the

outdoor task.

• Learners are guided to play

adapted games using any

functional part of the body and

adapted play materials as they

mention parts of plant. Learners

with difficulties in movement

could use mobility devices.

Learners with severe

manipulation and movement

difficulties could record the

scores or keep the play time as

time keepers.

80
